pr_body:
Certificate chains require subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.subjectDN.
Each adjacent certificate must satisfy this relationship, or else they
fail certificate chain validation.

CertGenUtils was setting subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.issuerDN.
That was incorrect. If the issuerCert was for a root CA, then issuerCert
had the same value for issuerCert.subjectDN = issuerCert.issuerDN, and
it was not possible to detect the bug.

For testing, use a subordinate CA to create a TLS certificate. A
subordinate CA has different values for its issuerCert.subjectDN !=
issuerCert.issuerDN. When the TLS certificate is created, it becomes
possible to assert subjectCert.issuerDN = issuerCert.subjectDN for the
TLS certificate.

Closes #69403
pr_title: TLS: Fix issuerDN for created certificates
